_doc: Standalone Watt Toolkit lifecycle test, ROUND 3 (handoff/TO_DSH.md re-run). Scope limited to starting and stopping the local accelerator; no BuildReasonSeg model work and no Task 6C. Read-only with respect to system configuration: DSH never edited the hosts file, the registry, the certificate store, PATH or the system proxy, and never force-killed a process. Every hosts change below was written by Watt Toolkit itself.

configuration_change_since_round_2._doc: The user also turned OFF 'minimize to tray on startup' and kept 'start acceleration automatically'.
configuration_change_since_round_2.reading: MinimizeOnStartup=false means the main window is expected to appear on launch; ProgramStartupRunProxy=true means acceleration is enabled automatically; ProxyMode=Hosts means acceleration rewrites the hosts file.

executable.note: unchanged across all three rounds: Microsoft Store MSIX 3.1.2025.0, entry point Steam++.exe, capabilities internetClient/runFullTrust/allowElevation

startup.main_page_evidence: screen capture shows the Watt Toolkit window in the foreground with 首页 (home) selected in the left sidebar, the welcome banner and the 最新消息 feed; the window also raises its own toast '加速已启动成功' (acceleration started successfully)

question_1_window_pops_up_on_launch.answer: YES - the main page appears on its own and takes the foreground
question_1_window_pops_up_on_launch.evidence: the 'Watt Toolkit' window existed 1663 ms after launch (1749 ms in the confirmation cycle), visible, not offscreen, and was the foreground window; the capture shows the home page with 首页 selected plus the app's own '加速已启动成功' toast

question_2_acceleration_works.answer: YES - automatically, with no GUI interaction
question_2_acceleration_works.evidence: Steam++.Accelerator.exe took 0.0.0.0:443/:80 within 18.7 s; hosts grew to 214 lines; git ls-remote OK, Hugging Face api/models 200 (15509 B) and config.json 200 (1505 B)

question_3_window_close_exits_fully.answer: YES, but only through the real window-close command
question_3_window_close_exits_fully.evidence: SC_CLOSE (what the title-bar X and Alt+F4 send) produced a full exit and restored the hosts file, twice; a bare WM_CLOSE from .NET CloseMainWindow() was ignored again

question_4_state_restored.evidence: 0 processes, 0 listeners on 443/80/26561/8868/7890/10808/10809, hosts byte-identical (efbbbf0d0a), system proxy still disabled, huggingface.co unresolvable again

three_round_comparison._doc: The same lifecycle test run three times with different Watt Toolkit tray/startup settings.

rounds.window_on_launch: no window (minimized to tray); a second activation surfaced it
rounds.bare_wm_close: hid the window to tray; accelerator kept running

rounds.window_on_launch: no visible window; a second activation surfaced it
window pops up by itself in ~1.7 s and takes the foreground

three_round_comparison.conclusion: TrayIcon controls whether a close request hides the window; MinimizeOnStartup controls whether the main page is shown at launch. Neither affects automatic acceleration. With TrayIcon=false the whole lifecycle is automatable, and the round-3 settings give the best behaviour: visible main page on launch plus a fully automatable exit.

classification.definition: DSH can start Watt Toolkit, acceleration enables itself, connectivity can be verified, acceleration can be stopped, Watt can be exited and cleanup can be verified - all without user interaction.
classification.caveat: the reliable exit path is the real window-close command (WM_SYSCOMMAND/SC_CLOSE), not the .NET CloseMainWindow() default, which posts a bare WM_CLOSE that this build ignores.
classification.future_workflow: DSH starts Watt Toolkit (the main page appears by itself), waits for the accelerator to take :443/:80, does the networked work, then sends SC_CLOSE to the 'Watt Toolkit' window and verifies the hosts file and ports are back to baseline. No user action required.

user_interaction_required.for_future_runs: none; the cycle is fully automatable with TrayIcon disabled

safety_warnings: None outstanding: the machine is back at its pre-test baseline (byte-identical hosts file, no Watt processes, no Watt listeners, system proxy still disabled).

While acceleration is on, Watt intercepts TLS. Python clients using the standard certifi bundle fail certificate verification; git and WinHTTP succeed because they use the Windows trust store. Do not fix this by injecting certificates into certifi.
This build ignores a bare WM_CLOSE, so a programmatic CloseMainWindow() leaves Watt running invisibly; use the real window close (X / Alt+F4) or send WM_SYSCOMMAND/SC_CLOSE.
limitations: The app exposes no UI Automation tree, so in-app controls still cannot be invoked by name; the exit used is the operating system's window-close command, which is what a user's X click sends.
The bare-WM_CLOSE-is-ignored behaviour is specific to Watt Toolkit 3.1.2025.0 and should be re-checked after an app update.
GitHub reachability remains intermittent at the network level (github.com resolves to a black-holed address) independently of Watt.
